findings.claim: VASP writes AECCAR0 and AECCAR1 on the starting (POSCAR) geometry and CHGCAR, AECCAR2, ELFCAR and LOCPOT on the final one, so in every relaxation run the archive's single lattice/positions (taken from CHGCAR, the first file read) do not describe its all_electron_core_density and superposed_atomic_density fields. Nothing in the sidecar records this, and the floors that read superposed_atomic_density (floors.Superposed_Atomic_Density_Errors, deep_dft/floors.py) treat it as the superposition of the stored structure. For the one run without CHGCAR (supercell shear_xy_g0.010) the archive geometry itself comes from AECCAR0, i.e. the starting geometry, beside a final-geometry localization field.
findings.counter: aeccar_evidence.py on diamond/triads_defects/Li-B-P/c8-c53-c1/config2/GGA-PBE (archive defect_set/8c7513908f838bdd): AECCAR0 and AECCAR1 header positions sit 0.0000 A from POSCAR and 1.0934 A from CONTCAR, while CHGCAR, AECCAR2, ELFCAR and LOCPOT sit 0.0000 A from CONTCAR. The grid values follow the headers: Li atom moved 1.093 A -> AECCAR0 3.426e+04 at the initial nucleus vs 1.072 at the final one, AECCAR1 588.8 vs 59.1, AECCAR2 177.6 vs 1179; P atom moved 0.570 A -> AECCAR0 5.861e+06 vs 97.4, AECCAR1 3.579e+04 vs 263. The archive's positions are 0.0000 A from CONTCAR and 1.0934 A from POSCAR. Store-wide (disp_counts.py): the AECCAR1 header geometry differs from the CHGCAR geometry by >0.001 A in 173/182 alloy, 120/196 defect and 90/170 supercell runs, and by >0.1 A in 130 alloy and 68 defect runs.
findings.fix: Record the AECCAR0/AECCAR1 header geometry beside those two fields (for example superposition_positions) and flag in the sidecar every run whose AECCAR0/1 geometry differs from CHGCAR's; score superposition floors only where the superposition sits on the density's geometry (static runs, or the chained static partner's AECCAR1), and replace the comment with 'AECCAR0 and AECCAR1 carry the starting geometry; the others carry the final one'.
findings.quote: # every volumetric file repeats the same geometry, so the first one read wins
findings.status: confirmed; reproduced by a second route: yes; conductor re-check: confirmed; fix: 4ea1b1a (F12)

findings.claim: The alloy superposed-atomic-density floor scores AECCAR1 built on the unrelaxed geometry against the relaxed density in 173 of 182 runs, so the reported median and spread include relaxation displacement rather than only the missing bonding; wherever the corpus holds the superposition on the relaxed geometry, the error is lower by up to 3.45 points. The line overstates the floor that structure-to-field members and the alloy transfer axis are scored against.
findings.counter: sad_alloy_pairs.py: on the nine pipeline pairs, where the stage-3 POSCAR is byte-identical to the stage-2 CONTCAR (same POTCAR sha and same grid in the census), scoring the stage-2 density against the relaxed-geometry superposition (stage-3 AECCAR1) instead of its own pre-relaxation AECCAR1 gives 27.46->25.98, 27.67->24.81, 25.93->23.49, 23.90->21.99, 22.47->20.25, 21.69->18.24, 17.68->15.81, 13.90->12.91 % (x=0, atoms moved only 0.007 A: 27.03->27.00, confirming the two AECCAR1 files differ only by geometry). disp_counts.py: 173 of the 182 alloy runs carry AECCAR1 on a geometry more than 0.001 A from the density's, 130 by more than 0.1 A. superposition_lines.py reproduces the reported line exactly from the store.
findings.fix: Recompute the floor with each run's superposition placed on its density's own geometry (built on /Pool from the POTCAR radial densities, or restricted to runs whose AECCAR1 geometry matches CHGCAR's) and restate the line; until then label it as measured against the pre-relaxation superposition.
findings.quote: - alloy_ensemble: median 27.02%, interquartile 3.64%, runs 182
findings.status: confirmed; reproduced by a second route: yes; conductor re-check: confirmed; fix: 4ea1b1a (F12)

findings.claim: The defect-campaign superposition floor mixes geometries in 120 of 196 runs; correcting just 57 of them already more than halves the reported interquartile range and lowers the median, so the line's spread (and to a lesser degree its median) measures relaxation displacement, not bonding.
findings.counter: sad_defect_substitution.py: as stage 0 computes it -> median 14.96%, interquartile 1.29%, runs 196; giving only the 57 chained PBE relaxations the superposition their static HSE partner carries on the relaxed geometry (partner POSCAR byte-identical to the PBE CONTCAR, one ionic step, same POTCAR sha) -> median 14.88%, interquartile 0.53%. findings.fix: Recompute with the superposition on each density's geometry (partner AECCAR1 for chained runs, POTCAR-built superposition on /Pool for the rest, or restrict to static runs) and restate the line.

findings.claim: For every relaxation run AECCAR1 is not the superposition of the structure whose density the members predict, so the SAD baseline does need construction (or a static partner) for those runs; the same assumption is repeated in section 9.6 ('already on disk as AECCAR1 for all 547') and in III.1's Gate A.

In 24 OUTCARs sampled across all six campaigns (four per campaign) the TITEL count equals the POSCAR species count every time.

findings.claim: Cartesian coordinates are converted to fractions without the scaling factor, so any Cartesian POSCAR/CONTCAR with scale != 1 (or a negative volume scale) would be read at wrong positions.
findings.counter: VASP POSCAR convention (VASP Wiki, 'POSCAR'; ASE's ase.io.vasp.read_vasp implements it as atoms_pos *= lattice_constant when cartesian): Cartesian positions are multiplied by the universal scaling factor of line 2, like the lattice vectors. Read_Geometry scales only the lattice, so a header with scale 2.0, unit lattice rows and 'Cartesian 0.5 0.5 0.5' comes back as fractional 0.25 where the convention gives 0.5. The synthetic test uses scale 1.0 and cannot see it. No corpus file is affected: all 5084 POSCAR and 5064 CONTCAR files are Direct (coordinate_modes.py).
findings.fix: Multiply Cartesian coordinates by the (possibly volume-derived) scale before converting to fractions, and add a scale != 1 Cartesian case to the synthetic test.
findings.quote: # cartesian and direct both come home as fractions

findings.claim: The canon's leakage rule for the parameter-to-field pattern (which includes lattice to charge density on the Perovskite Grid) says exact symmetry copies must not be split apart, but the committed perovskite 5-fold map places exact rotated or reflected copies of every fold-0 evaluation run in the training folds; the fold-0 'interpolation' numbers reported for II.1b and I.4 stage 1 are measured on that split, and no reason is recorded.
findings.counter: The perovskite runs whose three factors are permutations of each other (and, in the angle sweep, those related by taking the supplement of two angles, factor 0.8<->1.2 and 0.9<->1.1) are exactly degenerate: the angle stratum's 125 units fall into 14 classes whose census total energies agree to 0.56 micro-eV, the length stratum's 124 units into 34 classes agreeing to 1.09 micro-eV. The committed fold map treats every run as its own unit (Perovskite_Units), so all 25 fold-0 units of each stratum have an exact copy in folds 1-4. At field level: fold-0 alpha_0p8 equals fold-4 alpha_1p2 reflected along one lattice axis to relative L2 6.31e-07 and fold-3 beta_0p8 with a<->b swapped to 5.17e-07; length a_0p8 (fold 4) equals b_0p8 (fold 2) with a<->b swapped to 2.20e-07.
findings.fix: Build perovskite units from exact symmetry classes (sorted length factors; for the angle sweep, permutations plus the supplement of two angles) and hand folds to classes, then regenerate perovskite_folds.json and re-score the fold-0 perovskite entries.
findings.quote: exact symmetry degeneracy makes naive random splits test-on-train

findings.claim: The factor holdouts are extrapolation in the input coordinates only; on the angle sweep a held-out 0.8 structure is the mirror image of a trained 1.2 structure, so by the canon's own leakage rule these rows are mostly recall of seen structures, not extrapolation, and the sentence 'Under extrapolation the fixed bases degrade...' reads a symmetry-recall test as an extrapolation test.

Only the length stratum's holdouts have no such copies (0 of 61). operators/deep_operator_network/report.md titles the same blocks 'perovskite angle stratum, extrapolation'.

findings.claim: 28 of the 296 orbits (all two- and three-angle shear orbits) merge structures that are not symmetry-equivalent: the signed permutations act on a first-order symmetric tensor built from the point names, while the corpus deformation is a non-symmetric simple shear whose second-order terms break the equivalence.
findings.counter: Census gap spread inside the code's orbits, per functional: two_angle_shear (9 orbits) worst 84.4 meV cheap / 71.3 meV accurate; three_angle_shear (19 orbits) worst 173.0 / 198.4 meV; every other family at most 0.1 meV. The corpus builds a simple shear x' = x + g y: the POSCAR lattices of shear_xy_xz, shear_xy_yz and shear_xz_yz at g1 = g2 = 0.1 give F = I + 0.1(xy + xz), I + 0.1(xy + yz), I + 0.1(xz + yz), whose F^T F eigenvalues [0.868226, 1.0, 1.151774], [0.865965, 1.005006, 1.149029], [0.868226, 1.0, 1.151774] show the middle one is no rotation of the others, yet all three share orbit +0.0000_+0.0000_+0.0000_+0.1000_+0.1000_+0.0000 (PBE gaps 2.7804, 2.8074, 2.8648 eV). Orbit +0.0000_+0.0000_+0.0000_+0.0600_+0.0600_+0.0300 holds three distinct structures (PBE total energies -18.026366, -18.026546, -18.026660 eV). Grouping by F^T F under the same 48 signed permutations gives 349 classes with worst spread 0.1 meV.
findings.fix: Docstring: 'the strain-atlas orbit map: exact symmetry classes for the axial, isotropic and one-angle shear points; the two- and three-angle shear orbits are first-order groupings that merge up to three inequivalent structures'. (Exact classes would need the orbit of F^T F, 349 classes, which changes the holdout.)

findings.claim: The 'extrapolation' label on both factor holdouts is wrong for 57 of the 61 angle-stratum test runs in each: an exact physical copy of each (the same crystal written in a mirrored or permuted cell, matching to 1e-5 relative L2) sits in the fixed-basis training set. Every fixed-basis holdout row, and the angle-stratum rows of canonical, are therefore scored mostly on crystals the member was trained on, so the kill and pass rows are not extrapolation results.
findings.counter: Holding out every factor-0.8 run does not hold out the factor-0.8 crystals. The 5-atom cell's fractional atomic basis (checked in the store; see the second evidence command) is invariant under axis permutations and axis reversals, and reversing one lattice vector turns two cell angles into their supplements (72 deg <-> 108 deg, i.e. factor 0.8 <-> 1.2). Measured: perovskite_a_1_b_1_c_1_alpha_0p8_beta_1_gamma_1_angle (tags ['holdout_factor_0p8']) vs perovskite_a_1_b_1_c_1_alpha_1p2_beta_1_gamma_1_angle (tags ['holdout_factor_1p2'], so in the 0.8 split's training pool): relative L2 0.302 as stored, 6.3e-07 after reversing grid axis 2. Over the whole split (perov_orbits.py): 'holdout_factor_0p8 | angle test: n, with exact twin in training pool, in fixed-basis train, in canonical train = (61, 57, 57, 54)'; same for 1p2 = (61, 57, 57, 57). Every claimed twin verified on the fields (perov_twin_verify.py): 'holdout_factor_0p8 angle test runs with a claimed twin in fixed-basis train: 57 | worst best-transform rel L2 between run and its twin: 1.13e-05' (same 57 / 1.13e-05 for holdout_factor_1p2).
findings.fix: Build the perovskite units as symmetry orbits (axis permutations x axis reversals; a reversal maps two angle factors f -> 2-f) before splitting, as test-suite.md section 3 / 9.2 require. Re-split the two holdouts so that no held-out crystal's twin trains, or drop the 57 twinned angle runs. Until then, label these rows as not extrapolation in report.md and operator-results.md.
findings.note: 57 of 61 angle-stratum holdout runs have a physical copy (mirrored or permuted cell) in training; the label follows the canon's split definition, so the rows are not mislabeled against the canon but are not physical extrapolation; review item R1 (confirmed by the conductor on 2 October)

findings.claim: The per-voxel standardized loss does not work on the deviation the gate measures. It reweights voxels by inverse training variance and down-weights the high-variance voxels that dominate the gate's relative L2.
findings.counter: loss_weighting.py uses the driver's 80-run statistics on the 20 validation runs. The top 5% of voxels by raw deviation from the mean carry 56.9% of the raw squared deviation, which is what the gate's relative L2 measures, but only 6.2% of the standardized loss. The top 20% carry 89.3% against 23.4%. The loss weights each voxel's deviation by 1/sigma^2.
findings.fix: '... now works on the lattice-dependent deviation weighted by each voxel's inverse training variance, which de-emphasizes the high-variance voxels that dominate the gate's relative L2'.
findings.note: the spec's sentence that zero in standardized space is the training-mean field is right; what stands is the unstated loss/metric mismatch: inverse-variance weighting down-weights the high-variance voxels that dominate the gate's relative L2

findings.claim: Normalizing K and V instead of Q and K makes the attention Galerkin-type, not softmax-free. The Fourier-type normalizes Q and K and is softmax-free too.
findings.counter: Cao (NeurIPS 2021) defines two softmax-free attentions. The Fourier-type, z = (Q~ K~^T) V / n, normalizes Q and K. The Galerkin-type, z = Q (K~^T V~) / n, normalizes K and V. Both drop the softmax. Which pair is normalized decides Galerkin-type versus Fourier-type, and doing the K^T V product first makes it linear in n.
findings.fix: 'normalizing K and V rather than Q and K is what makes it the Galerkin-type rather than the Fourier-type attention; both drop the softmax.'
findings.quote: rather than Q and K is what makes the map softmax-free.

findings.claim: In every attention layer, the kernel's value projection and the layer's local linear term start from identical weights and biases. Both are linear maps of the same input, so their initializations are not independent.
findings.counter: GalerkinAttentionKernel(seed=k) seeds value_projection with k + 2. The kernel is built at k = seed + 4*layer_index + 1, so its value projection gets seed + 4*layer_index + 3, the same seed as local_linear. On the gate member (seed 20260916) the check prints [True, True, True, True]: weights and biases are equal in all four layers.
findings.fix: Allocate five seeds per layer, e.g. kernel seed + 5*layer_index + 1 and local_linear seed + 5*layer_index + 5, and shift the decoder seed to match.

findings.claim: The comment says no operator on coarse input can beat the truncation null. That is false: the truth's content above the coarse band can be a function of the coarse input, and a pointwise nonlinear map recovers it exactly (skill 1.0). The null is a reference level, not a floor. The axis reports a skill because the model can beat it. The same unbeatable-floor claim is repeated in test_invariance.py ('an operator handed only the coarse input cannot beat carrying the coarse truth back up'; '# the null is the floor of the axis') and in test-suite.md section 9.5(a) ('the irreducible truncation floor').

A pointwise nonlinearity regenerates the truth's harmonics above the coarse band from coarse input alone, so it beats the null.
findings.fix: Reword to '# the null is the coarse truth carried back up, what a map adding nothing above the coarse band would score'. Remove the 'cannot beat' and 'floor of the axis' wording from test_invariance.py's Test_A_Resampler_Sits_Exactly_On_The_Truncation_Null docstring and comment.

findings.claim: The implicit rule silently returns a divergent partial sum instead of the exact adjoint whenever a converged equilibrium is non-contractive; commit e5e8d65 also misdescribes it as solving 'by the same kind of fixed-point iteration the forward already uses' (the forward is damped and Anderson-mixed, the adjoint is neither).
findings.counter: The adjoint 'solve' is the undamped Neumann iteration u <- J^T u + g, stopped at iteration_cap with nothing recorded, so it diverges whenever the spectral radius of J at the equilibrium is >= 1, which the damped, Anderson-accelerated forward can still converge on. Probe map (zero kernel, local matrix -3·I, bias (0.3, -0.2), uniform input): forward cap_was_hit False, final_residual 7.9e-04; J at the equilibrium spans -1.81 to -1.26; the implicit rule returns a bias gradient of [6.2e+08, -2.5e+03] against the exact implicit-function-theorem gradient [1.816, -1.240] (u = g/(1-J) for this diagonal map).
findings.fix: Solve (I - J^T) u = g with the forward's own damped Anderson scheme (or a Krylov solve on the VJP) and record or raise when the adjoint has not met the tolerance by the cap.
findings.note: the implicit adjoint is a plain Neumann iteration with no convergence check: a converged but non-contractive equilibrium returns a divergent partial sum silently (relative gap 7e10 on the auditor's probe); training-path code, so a review item R16, not clear-cut

findings.claim: The spec says a test orbit counts as covered only if every one of its runs is inside the band. report.py:402 does something else: it scores each orbit as the median of its runs' covered indicators (Median_Per_Unit) and then averages over orbits. The only way to reach 0.977 is 21.5/22 (43/44 = 0.97727), meaning 21 orbits at 1 and one orbit at 0.5, where half its runs fall outside the band. findings.claim: Calibrate first reduces each unit's run scores to their median (self.unit_scores = Median_Per_Unit(Nonconformity_Scores(...), unit_keys)) and only then takes the conformal rank. So the band that Coverage_Guarantee reports, and that the calibrator exposes as coverage_guarantee_low/high, holds for one event only: a new unit's median run lands inside the band. When a unit holds several runs, neither the marginal coverage of a run (the usual meaning of marginal coverage) nor the coverage of a whole unit is guaranteed. The only coverage tests (test_parts Test_The_Calibrated_Interval_Covers_Held_Out_Units_At_Its_Level and test_residual_correction's point-prediction test) use Lone_Orbits, one run per unit, where the median changes nothing. The IV.1 spec reads the guarantee as covering every run of an orbit. The IV.1 test block has several runs per orbit (88 runs over 22 orbits), and its 21.5/22 coverage shows that the runs of one orbit did not all score alike.
findings.counter: median_unit_coverage.py (23 calibration orbits of 4 runs each, independent run scores, 4000 trials): stated guarantee band at 23 units: [0.900, 0.942]; new orbit's median run covered: 0.922; a run of a new orbit covered: 0.790; every run of a new orbit covered: 0.401
findings.fix: Either reduce each unit to its largest run score (max, not median), which makes the guarantee cover every run of a unit (the same sup rule the field score already follows over voxels), or state in Coverage_Guarantee and ConformalCalibrator that the guaranteed event is the unit's median run. The multiple-input member, whose branches are two-channel, builds its own inspection function to get around it. The encoder is left unreachable through Inspect, against the inspection doctrine in operators/README.md.
findings.counter: projection_encoder_inspect.py: 'projection works: (3,)' then 'Inspect raises ValueError: cannot reshape array of size 128 into shape (4,4,4)'; the multiple-input spec records the same: 'BasisProjectionEncoder.Inspect() assumes a single-channel field, and this member's two branches'
findings.fix: Record the field's full value shape, channels included, and reshape the mean to it and the modes to (rank, *that shape); split per channel for rendering.
findings.quote: state["basis_mean"] = self.basis_mean.reshape(self.last_grid_shape)

findings.claim: The guards 'if branch_coefficients.ndim == 2 and branch_coefficients.shape[0] != channel_count:' (readouts line 167) and the NonlinearDecoder twin (line 383) check only two-dimensional branches. findings.claim: Frequency_Split_Relative_L2 does not return the relative L2 of each band. Modes on the last axis's kz=0 and Nyquist planes weigh twice as much as every other mode, so the value depends on which axis the error lies along, and it does not reproduce Relative_L2 when the band is the whole field. Every frequency_split_relative_l2_low/high row in operators/deep_operator_network/report.md was computed this way (for example the principal_component fold-0 member at 0.016584 / 0.122894). On real perovskite floor predictions the per-run bias reaches 11-16%.
findings.counter: Band_Error sums np.linalg.norm over the np.fft.rfftn half-spectrum without doubling the interior last-axis modes (each stands for itself and its unstored conjugate), so modes on the kz=0 and Nyquist planes count double. Output, 8^3 truth cos(2πx)+cos(2πz): an error of 0.1cos(2πz) gives 0.0577 and the same error along x gives 0.0816, while the band's true relative L2 is 0.1/√2 = 0.0707. With cutoff 1e9 (the whole field is the 'low' band) it returns 0.27616 where Relative_L2 of the same pair is 0.27768. On the perovskite fold-0 nearest-angle copy floor (cutoff 8) the low-band median is 0.078624 as coded against 0.085226 full-spectrum, with the worst run off by 16.3%; on the ridge floor 0.039214 against 0.040418, per-run ratio 0.887 to 1.075.
findings.fix: Weight half-spectrum entries by 2 except on the kz=0 plane and, for even n, the Nyquist plane (or use np.fft.fftn with the full-grid radius). Add a test that an infinite cutoff reproduces Relative_L2, then regenerate the DeepONet frequency-split rows.
findings.quote: relative L2 error of the below-cutoff and above-cutoff mode bands
findings.status: confirmed; reproduced by a second route: yes; conductor re-check: confirmed

findings.claim: The perovskite split makes every run its own exchangeable unit. The 5-atom cell (Nb at the origin, Ag at the body center, O at the three half-edge sites) is symmetric under axis permutation, so runs whose lattice-factor triples are permutations of each other are exact rotated copies of one field. The split scatters these copies across folds, so every fold-0 evaluation run has an exact copy in the training folds, which contradicts the plan's orbit rule in 9.2 ('any random split is invalid by construction'). This was checked field by field for all 25 fold-0 angle runs; for the length stratum it follows from orbit membership, with sample pairs checked field by field. The unit counts are overstated too: 25 'units' are 19 orbits. The perovskite interpolation rows (DeepONet II.1b 'pass/pass', the Galerkin copy and interpolation floors) and their unit counts rest on this split.
findings.counter: Every one of the 25 fold-0 angle-stratum runs has a run in folds 1-4 whose angle triple is a permutation of its own. After the matching grid-axis transpose, the two charge densities differ by at most 8.30e-06 relative L2 (for example alpha 0.8 beta 0.9 gamma 1, fold 4, against alpha 0.9 beta 0.8 gamma 1, fold 3: 3.4e-07). The 25 fold-0 'units' are 19 permutation orbits. The angle stratum's 125 runs form 35 orbits and the length stratum's 124 runs form 34, and every fold-0 length run also has an orbit partner in folds 1-4. The length pair a0.8 b0.9 c1 (fold 2, grid 56x60x64) against a0.9 b0.8 c1 (fold 1, grid 60x56x64) differs by 3.1e-07. scoring.py's Unit_Medians promises 'each exchangeable unit's own median, so symmetry copies inside one orbit count once'.
findings.fix: Key perovskite units by stratum plus the sorted factor triple (the permutation orbit), re-assign folds by orbit, and regenerate the perovskite rows, unit counts and verdicts.
findings.quote: one unit per perovskite run, with the duplicated center removed
findings.status: confirmed; reproduced by a second route: yes; conductor re-check: confirmed

findings.claim: The degenerate gap_edge_error (floors 0.000000, member 1.9125) is not a limit of the support-edge read-out. The reference energy is placed at the valence-band maximum, the band edge itself, so the read-out's 'empty side' begins inside the smeared valence tail. With a mid-gap reference the same read-out recovers each run's gap with r = 0.998. The report's explanation, repeated on operator-results.md ('an artifact of the smearing on this window'), misattributes a wrong argument to the metric and the smearing, and the printed gap_edge_error values do not measure band-edge placement.
findings.counter: The report's call is Gap_Edge_Error(predicted_curve, truth_curve, self.energy_grid), which leaves gap_reference at its default 0.0. On these grids 0.0 is the valence-band maximum. On the 248 strain_to_states test truths that default reads every conduction edge at 0.02 eV, and the support gap has a median of 0.060 eV. Setting gap_reference to half each run's occupancy-walk gap, the same Gap_Edge_Energies reads a support gap with median 3.660 eV and a correlation of 0.998 with the occupancy-walk gap (median 4.075 eV).
findings.fix: Pass gap_reference = half the truth's occupancy-walk gap (or a fixed in-gap energy), recompute gap_edge_error for the floors, member and ablation, and rewrite the paragraph and the results-page sentence.
findings.quote: that is the metric's own limit, not a physics failure

findings.claim: The test asserts that the median lies inside [confidence_low, confidence_high]. The bounds are a bootstrap interval for the mean of the unit medians, so this is not a property of the statistic. The test passes only because its four unit medians (0.055, 0.075, 0.095, 0.115) are symmetric, and committed artifacts break the invariant it asserts. findings.claim: The resumed path trusts any probe manifest it finds. Nothing records whether the probe passed, so a relaunch after a failed probe skips the probe and trains all three stages from that probe's checkpoint parameters. Two cases: the process died between the failed peak-rate probe and the retry (the manifest then holds the rejected peak rate), or both probes failed and raised RuntimeError (the manifest then holds 0.3 x peak).
findings.counter: The resume branch reads only json.loads(probe_manifest_path.read_text())["learning_rate"] (staged.py:65); no verdict is stored anywhere. A probe manifest on the pool holds exactly: best_step, best_validation_score, completed_steps, device, engine, final_loss, hook_present, learning_rate, parameter_names, patience, resumed_from_step, run_name, seed, step_count, stopped_early, validation_interval, validation_unit_count, wall_clock_seconds, working_precision (no verdict). Train writes that manifest (loop.py:346) before Staged_Training calls Sane_Loss_Curve (staged.py:76 and 83), so a probe that failed its check still leaves a manifest behind.
findings.fix: Write a separate verdict record only after Sane_Loss_Curve passes, and on resume refuse to continue unless it says sane. Otherwise, correct the comment to say only the rate is read back.

findings.claim: Spacing flat indices evenly aliases with the grid. On power-of-two cube grids the held-out points collapse onto one or two planes. The validation score that picks each stage's best parameters, and DeepONet's step-count candidate, is therefore measured on a biased slice: for the perovskite angle stratum it is a single plane through the atoms whose mean density is about 1.8x the field mean. Test_A_Fixed_Spread_Covers_A_Field_And_Never_Repeats checks only that the indices are distinct and in range, not coverage.
findings.counter: On a (64, 64, 64) field the 512 evenly spaced flat indices take 64 values on the first axis, 8 on the second and 1 on the third, so every held-out point lies in one plane. On (80, 80, 80) they cover 2 planes, and on (40, 40, 40) 8 of 40. DeepONet's lattice fold-0 canonical run uses the default 512 points (deep_operator_network/report.py, Perovskite_Canonical_Member), and 20 of its 39 validation units are angle-stratum 64^3 fields. On the first five of those, the 512 points average 1.464-1.542 e/A^3 against whole-field means of 0.785-0.848, with spread 1.914-1.937 against 1.523-1.567.
findings.fix: Choose held-out points per axis (a strided sub-grid, or a fixed low-discrepancy set of fractional coordinates rounded to the grid) or draw them once from a fixed seed. Add a coverage test on 64^3 and 80^3 grids.
findings.quote: a fixed spread of flattened positions across a field, so a held batch needs no seed of its own

findings.claim: The reduced-salted floor row's interquartile (11.583332) and 95% mean interval ([2.832035, 7.337816]) are not a spread of ridge corrections but the product of a construction defect: every fold-zero run carrying an element absent from the training folds gets a near-uniform +8.40 e/A^3 offset (about twelve times the mean density), so all 9 held-out-chemistry units score 11.4-12.0 normalized MAE while the other 12 score 0.09-0.11.
findings.counter: Recomputing the floor with the member's own ridge, sampler and seeds (shell features from a vectorized copy of floors.Species_Shell_Features, calibrated to 2e-16 relative against the original) reproduces the row: median 0.111713, interquartile 11.583337, interval [2.832036, 7.337819]. Per-unit medians: the 12 units whose elements all occur in folds 1-4 score 0.0931-0.1127; the 9 held-out-chemistry units (dopants Cu, Rh, Bi, Tl, Fr, Sc, Ba, I, Al, each with 0 training runs) score 11.41-12.01. On every held-out run the ridge correction averages +8.40 e/A^3 over the cell (cell-mean density 0.70 e/A^3). Mechanism (salted_mechanism.py): the fitted raw intercept is 537.78 e/A^3 = 64 x 8.40, cancelled on 64-atom training structures by per-atom shell terms (each element's 3.0 A shell coefficient times 1/V is about -13.3; carbon -13.24); Species_Shell_Features drops an atom whose element is not in the vocabulary (element_column_of.get(symbol, -1)), so one atom's share stays uncancelled. Controls: scoring the unseen atom as a carbon column gives NMAE 0.10-0.24 on those runs (SAD alone 0.15-0.32); raising the ridge penalty from the default 1e-6 to 0.01 gives 0.259 on run a9d5ea28a3138aa9 (11.67 as built). With the offset removed (salted_alternatives.py) the same floor has interquartile 0.009-0.029 and interval [0.104-0.111, 0.123-0.136]; the median only moves to 0.108-0.111.
findings.fix: Remove the common-mode blow-up before re-measuring: use a real ridge penalty on the standardized design (1e-6 against a Gram diagonal of order 1e5 is ordinary least squares), and/or give atoms of elements outside the vocabulary a fallback (e.g. host or pooled) shell column instead of silently dropping them; then regenerate the row. Expected: interquartile about 0.01-0.03, interval about [0.10, 0.14], median 0.108-0.111, gate b bar 0.036-0.037 instead of 0.037238.
findings.note: the report flags the spread but attributes it to ridge ill-conditioning on 'a handful' of units; the cause is a construction defect (a near-uniform +8.4 e/A^3 offset on every unit whose element is absent from training, 9 of 21), so the recording is partial and wrong about the mechanism
findings.quote: "interquartile": 11.583332
findings.status: confirmed; reproduced by a second route: yes; defense: recorded (after the result); conductor re-check: confirmed

findings.claim: The lone dopant atom of both IVA-element-single-impurity/Si runs (fold zero) is a silicon atom in the calculation, but the species handling labels it hydrogen: the embedding sends it to the unknown row and the reduced-salted and nearest-copy floors score it with hydrogen shells and a hydrogen composition. Matching titles to the species column by name, 'not by position', is exactly what VASP does not do.
findings.counter: Census rows for the two runs whose dopant the member keys as H: diamond/single_defect/IVA-element-single-impurity/Si/GGA-PBE and .../Si/HSE06 have POSCAR species line ['H', 'C'] with counts [1, 63], pseudopotentials Si then C (element symbols of the titles, in order), and NELECT 256.0000; the store's electron_count and the charge-density integral are 256.0 too. VASP assigns the POTCAR blocks to the POSCAR ion types by position (VASP Wiki, POTCAR: for several species the potentials are concatenated in the order the species appear in POSCAR), so the single type-1 atom was computed with the Si potential: 1 x 4 + 63 x 4 = 256 valence electrons, whereas a hydrogen atom would give 1 + 252 = 253. The store's species array still says H, the member routes it to the unknown row, and both floors score it as hydrogen: re-scoring with the Si label changes the reduced-salted values of 34c5ebd36d43713f / bd39ceefa779d83c from 0.1016 / 0.1058 to 0.1004 / 0.1016 and the nearest-copy values from 0.0298 / 0.0326 to 0.0651 / 0.0666 (silicon_relabel.py); the pooled medians do not move.

Measured with the member's own Drawn_Probe_Points on a 6-atom, 5 A cubic test cell and a field peaked on the atoms: self-normalized mean / truth = 1.136 +- 0.006 at 4 probes and 1.032 +- 0.003 at 16, while (1/(nV)) sum w f gives 0.993 +- 0.003 and 0.999 +- 0.002. findings.claim: The magnetization loss normalizes by a noise-level integrated moment for zero-moment runs, so a batch drawing one of them is dominated by fitting numerical noise by ten to twelve orders of magnitude.
findings.counter: Of the member's 109 training runs (folds 2-4), 29 have zero net moment (|final_magnetization| <= 1e-3) but pass the 1e-6 mask; 13 of them have an integrated |m| of only 1.06e-6 to 1.68e-5 Bohr magnetons (numerical noise). Their magnetization residuals are divided by that integral, so their magnetization term is weighted (2.13 / 1.68e-5)^2 = 1.6e10 to (2.13 / 1.06e-6)^2 = 4.1e12 times that of the median magnetic run (integrated |m| 2.13). Commit 2b6809f promised the mask removes runs whose moment is 'too small for the loss's own normalization to be meaningful'.
findings.fix: Mask the magnetization term by a physical moment threshold (e.g. the gate-C selection |final_magnetization| > 1e-3, or integral |m| > 0.05 Bohr magnetons, the census's magnetic cut), or floor the normalizer at such a value.

findings.claim: The species key for the Si-impurity fold-zero unit is wrong. The loader trusts the stale H label in the species column over the title order that VASP actually used. The nearest-copy and reduced-salted floor values for that unit (1 of 21 fold-zero units) are therefore computed on the wrong chemistry, and the member would embed a Si atom through the untrained unknown row.
findings.counter: The two fold-zero runs diamond/single_defect/IVA-element-single-impurity/Si/{GGA-PBE,HSE06} (34c5ebd36d43713f, bd39ceefa779d83c) store species C x63 + H x1, but their titles name Si and C, and the census gives o_nelect 256.0000 (the store's electron_count is 256.0 and the density integrates to 256.0). 63 carbons x 4 valence electrons + 4 = 256 means the impurity was computed with the Si pseudopotential; an H impurity would give 63x4 + 1 = 253. VASP takes each ion's potential from POTCAR order, so the 'H' in the POSCAR species line is a stale label. Because the loader matches titles to that stale label, the Si impurity is keyed (unknown, unknown), even though Si is in the training vocabulary (six training runs carry Si). The floors read the same stale species_symbols: Nearest_Copy_Errors copies the H-impurity training run 123f0568753bb34e (diamond/single_defect/IA-element-single-impurity/H/gga-pbe) for both Si runs, and the reduced-salted ridge puts H shells on a Si site.
findings.fix: When a run's species set disagrees with the element set its titles name, resolve species by POSCAR/POTCAR position (cross-checked against NELECT), or correct the label in the store. Then rerun the floors for that unit.
findings.note: round 3: the species key for the silicon single-impurity unit follows the stale H label (K01, review item R8); the spec records the choice as deliberate but treats the stale label as the chemistry; reproduced by a second route
findings.quote: (symbol, title_by_element[symbol]) if symbol in title_by_element else UNKNOWN_SPECIES_KEY
findings.status: confirmed (round 3); reproduced by a second route: yes; defense: recorded

Neither Train_Deep_Dft_Member, Deep_Dft_Cached_Structures, Cached_Structure nor ProbeBatchSource calls it, and vocabulary indices are frozen at cache time (sampling.py Cached_Structure). Measured with arms.py: every one_angle_shear level holds 6 runs (shear_xy, shear_xz, shear_yz x PBE/HSE06) and every two_angle_shear level 6 runs (xy_xz, xy_yz, xz_yz pairs); 'levels mixing points' = 40/40 and 76/76. mix.py: shear_xy vs shear_xz at g=0.05 differ by 3.9% relative L2, and the 6-run level mean differs from each real run by 2.3% (g=0.05) to 4.5% (g=0.1). perrun_all.py: scored per run (same plane, same functional for level and corners) the bracketing floor median is one_angle_shear 9.87e-06 and two_angle_shear 2.53e-04, against the reported 0.000005 and 0.000194 (report.md table rows bracketing_interpolation_floor__one_angle_shear / __two_angle_shear relative_l2); other families agree to 3 digits.
findings.fix: Key shear levels by (plane or plane pair, values) — e.g. make each plane its own arm, or include the plane in the level — and re-score the floors per run; restate the one-angle and two-angle shear floor medians.

findings.claim: Every parametric level merges the PBE and HSE06 runs, so every leave-one-level-out floor (and the 0.064% kill bar) is computed on a functional-averaged field that is not any calculation's density; a functional-blind member scored per run has an irreducible error about seven times the bar, so the gate as built is either unpassable or will be scored on targets no run produces.

The member takes only the six strain components (PARAMETRIC_PARAMETER_COUNT = 6, lift (h, 31) = 6 + 25), so scored per run it cannot get below about 0.5% relative L2, while the kill bar set from these level-mean floors is 0.064%.

findings.claim: For 66 of the 423 arm-population levels the scored truth is an average of three differently oriented shear fields that no single strain tensor produces, while every tensor-based predictor (the member, Gaussian radial basis, ridge, nearest copy) is asked for the field of one orientation; the arm-population numbers for those families (e.g. gaussian_radial_basis_floor__one_angle_shear 0.016164, the member's pooled 0.002452 and its mean interval [0.005053, 0.006796]) carry an irreducible orientation-mixing error, not model error.
findings.counter: arm_roles.py: one_angle_shear (38 levels) and two_angle_shear (28 levels) have 6 runs per level whose strain tensors are NOT identical (('one_angle_shear', 6, False): 38, ('two_angle_shear', 6, False): 28). Strain_Level drops the shear plane, so one 'level' pools the xy, xz and yz shears (e.g. shear_xy_g-0.005, shear_xz_g-0.005, shear_yz_g-0.005). The truth Cached_Level_Field averages the three orientations, but the member, the RBF, ridge and copy floors are all queried at the tensor of runs_by_level[level][0] (the xy shear only). shear_mix.py: a perfect per-run predictor at that tensor would already score relative L2 against the orientation-averaged truth of median 0.0226 (one_angle_shear, 38 levels, range 0.0023-0.0429) and 0.0236 (two_angle_shear, 28 levels, range 0.0065-0.0487), roughly 10x the member's pooled 0.002452.
findings.fix: Key arm levels by the full strain tensor (or by plane plus magnitude) so each level's runs share one tensor, or score each run against its own field and tensor; regenerate the arm-population rows and verdicts.
findings.note: round 3: on 66 of the 423 arm levels the scored truth is the mean over three shear planes, and the member is handed the xy-plane tensor, so its arm rows carry an irreducible orientation-mixing error (an exact single-plane field scores median relative L2 0.023 against that truth); the fitted floors learn the averaged map, so the irreducibility claim does not extend to them; same mechanism as M7-manifold-decoder-005 and review item R17

findings.counter: Reference_Vector_Jacobian_Product(lambda x: x**2, np.asfortranarray(np.arange(6.0).reshape(2,3)), np.ones((2,3))) returns all zeros, while the same point in C order returns [[0,2,4],[6,8,10]]: np.array(point) keeps Fortran order (order='K'), so point_values.reshape(-1) is a copy and the perturbation is never seen (exp1.py, 'refvjp F-order' vs 'refvjp C-order').

findings.claim: The 48 grid operations are exact diamond symmetries only for an 8-atom conventional cell; on the 64-atom 2x2x2 supercell grids the members and the harness use, the 24 translated operations shift by twice the glide and are not symmetries of the crystal.
findings.counter: Diamond_Grid_Operations takes its translations from the 8-atom conventional motif (24 operations carry (1/4,1/4,1/4)), but every 80-cubed cubic-block grid the callers pass is a 64-atom supercell, i.e. 2x2x2 conventional cells (pristine run supercell_strains/049d8f7daec846ab: lattice 7.29989 A cubic, 64 atoms at multiples of 1/8). Applied there, the 24 translated operations move the pristine density by relative L2 0.8163 each (0.8336 / 0.8431 on the 40-cubed ELF of the pristine Converged_for_doping_analyze runs 78e29cde81149eca / ca08841df18b43df), while the same operations with the translation halved (the supercell's own glide, 1/8 of the grid) give at most 4.9e-08 (6.8e-04 on the ELF). On a synthetic 8-atom conventional cell all 48 are exact (max 1.4e-16). So on every grid the code is used on, half of the 'exact symmetry operations' are not symmetries of the structure; they are still isometries of the cubic cell (point operation plus a rigid 10-voxel shift), so augmentation remains valid, but the docstrings and the companion comment 'the glide translations are quarter cells, and a quarter cell is whole voxels only here' are wrong for the 64-atom cells (the glide there is an eighth of the grid).
findings.fix: Say in the docstrings that the translations are conventional-cell fractions; either divide the translation by the supercell multiple (2 for the 64-atom cells, which needs eighth-divisible grids) or state that the operations are cubic-cell isometries rather than crystal symmetries. Rewrite the Exactly_Operable_Grid comment accordingly.
findings.quote: """one exact symmetry operation on a compatible cubic grid"""

findings.claim: The pre-code test plan states that the glide translations are exact 20-voxel rolls on the 80-cubed grids; for the 64-atom cells those grids sample, the glide is a 10-voxel roll, and the code built from this sentence applies the wrong shift.
findings.counter: The 80-cubed grids of section 9.5(d) belong to the 64-atom supercell and defect runs, whose cell is 2x2x2 conventional cells (supercell_strains/049d8f7daec846ab lattice 7.29989 A, defect_set lattice 7.157 A, 64 atoms). The diamond glide is a quarter of the conventional cell, i.e. an eighth of this cell: a 10-voxel roll on 80 points. A 20-voxel roll (what Apply_Grid_Operation does with translation 0.25 on extent 80) leaves the pristine density at relative distance 0.8163 from itself; a 10-voxel roll gives 4.9e-08. The same wrong number appears at test-suite.md 'the non-symmorphic quarter-shifts are exact 20-point rolls' (V.1 data-volume paragraph).
findings.fix: Replace '20-voxel rolls' and '20-point rolls' with '10-voxel rolls (an eighth of the 2x2x2 supercell)', or say any whole-voxel shift is an isometry of the cubic cell so the glide need not be matched.
findings.quote: (quarter-shifts = exact 20-voxel rolls)

findings.claim: Augmented_Training_Pair applies cubic diamond operations to every training run, including the strained supercell_strains cells. On those cells the operations are not exact symmetries, and the Gram channels are not transformed with the field, so about 39% of augmented draws would be physically inconsistent training examples. Training has not run yet, so no reported number is affected.
findings.counter: The cubic block (operators/evaluation/localization_block.py CubicBlock) keeps every 80^3 run with no lattice filter. Of the 196 training runs (folds 2-4), 87 supercell_strains runs have non-cubic lattices (tetragonal stretch or a gamma != 90 shear). For 3,648 of the 9,408 (run, operation) pairs (38.8%), the drawn signed permutation M does not preserve the run's metric (M^T G M != G; worst relative change 0.198), so it is not a symmetry of that crystal. AugmentedMemberBatches.Next_Batch (alias_free_convolutional/report.py) also passes the run's unchanged gram_vector beside the rotated field, so the Gram channels describe a different cell than the augmented density and target.
findings.fix: Draw only the operations with M^T G M == G for the run's own lattice (or transform the Gram vector consistently and accept non-symmetric draws as new cells), and correct the docstring; or restrict augmentation to cubic-lattice runs.
findings.quote: """one exact grid symmetry, drawn once and applied identically to the input and its own target"""
